patient.chief_complaint: Found minimally responsive at home after witnessed brief shaking episode, now confused and agitated
patient.hpi: A 58-year-old White male retired electrician was brought to the emergency department by EMS after his wife called 911. She reported witnessing a brief generalized tonic-clonic seizure lasting approximately 90 seconds while he was sitting at the breakfast table. She noted he had been 'not himself' for the past three weeks — increasingly forgetful, having trouble with word-finding, and seeming confused in the mornings. After the witnessed seizure stopped, she expected him to recover within minutes as had occurred with prior episodes, but he remained minimally responsive and confused for over 25 minutes, prompting her call to 911. He has a known diagnosis of right temporal glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) diagnosed 8 months ago, status post gross total resection followed by concurrent temozolomide and radiation, now on maintenance temozolomide. He completed his most recent temozolomide cycle 11 days ago. He takes dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily for peritumoral edema, which was recently tapered from 6 mg twice daily over the past two weeks per his neuro-oncologist's instruction. He has a known seizure disorder secondary to his brain tumor and takes levetiracetam 1000 mg twice daily. His wife reports he has been taking his levetiracetam consistently. He denies fever, headache, or new neurological symptoms when he can communicate. Family history is notable for no inherited neurological conditions. Social history: former smoker (quit at diagnosis), occasional alcohol, married with adult children.

eeg.impression: ABNORMAL EEG. Non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) arising from right temporal-parietal region. Electrographic seizures characterized by evolving rhythmic theta with sharp waves, meeting modified Salzburg criteria for NCSE. LPDs in right temporal region between seizure runs suggest ongoing epileptiform burden. Clinical correlation recommended.

ct.impression: Post-surgical changes from right temporal GBM resection with known surgical cavity. No acute intracranial hemorrhage. Mild right hemisphere sulcal effacement. MRI with gadolinium required for assessment of tumor progression vs radiation changes.
recommended_actions: MRI brain with and without gadolinium for tumor recurrence vs radiation necrosis assessment

output.impression: Subtle right parietal cortical DWI changes likely represent ictal pseudostroke from active NCSE — NOT acute ischemic stroke; do NOT administer tPA. Left temporal lobe normal. Clinical correlation recommended.
Ongoing NCSE with partial response to benzodiazepine + lacosamide. Seizure burden reduced but not eliminated. Clinical correlation recommended.

interactions.description: Dexamethasone can mildly reduce levetiracetam levels via CYP enzyme induction — minor effect, monitoring recommended
interactions.clinical_recommendation: Levetiracetam levels are therapeutic; no dose change needed. Monitor levels if dexamethasone dose is substantially changed.

interactions.description: No clinically significant interaction between dexamethasone and lacosamide
interactions.clinical_recommendation: No dose adjustment needed for lacosamide

output.summary: No major interactions between current AEDs and dexamethasone. Mild pharmacokinetic effect possible but clinically insignificant at current levels. Dexamethasone escalation for tumor edema is safe and appropriate alongside AED regimen.

output.query: GBM recurrence management NCSE tumor-related epilepsy treatment

results.title: Management of tumor-related epilepsy in glioblastoma
results.key_finding: Levetiracetam remains first-line AED for GBM-related seizures. Lacosamide is effective add-on. Valproate has additional potential anti-tumor effect via HDAC inhibition. Tumor recurrence is the primary driver of breakthrough seizures — oncologic control essential.

results.title: NCSE in brain tumor patients: diagnosis and management
results.key_finding: NCSE in GBM patients is underdiagnosed; EEG essential. Steroid taper without adequate AED coverage increases breakthrough seizure risk. High rCBV on PWI distinguishes recurrence from radiation necrosis with 87% sensitivity.

output.summary: GBM recurrence with peritumoral edema is a recognized precipitant of NCSE. Steroid taper may have reduced edema control, unmasking epileptogenic tissue adjacent to recurrent tumor. Dual AED therapy is appropriate. Bevacizumab for recurrent GBM may also reduce seizure burden by anti-permeability effect.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Non-convulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) secondary to GBM recurrence with increased peritumoral edema following dexamethasone taper

differential.key_features: Autoimmune panel negative; clear structural etiology (GBM recurrence) explains NCSE; no psychiatric prodrome
Duration >25 minutes without recovery makes simple post-ictal state unlikely; EEG confirms ongoing electrographic seizure activity (NCSE)
Mild hyponatremia and hyperglycemia present but insufficient to explain NCSE in isolation; EEG shows focal ictal pattern not diffuse triphasic waves
High rCBV on perfusion MRI favors recurrence over radiation necrosis; timeline (8 months post-treatment, maintenance phase) consistent with recurrence

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Right temporal NCSE with LPDs meeting modified Salzburg criteria

optimal_actions.action: Administer IV lorazepam 2 mg IV as first-line treatment for NCSE; place IV access and monitor respiratory status
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Partial reduction in electrographic seizure burden on EEG

optimal_actions.action: Order emergent labs including AED levels, BMP, CBC, glucose, CK, lactate
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Levetiracetam therapeutic; mild hyponatremia; elevated lactate/CK post-ictal

optimal_actions.action: Perform non-contrast CT head to exclude hemorrhage
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Post-surgical changes only; no new hemorrhage

optimal_actions.action: Load IV lacosamide 400 mg IV over 30 minutes as second-line AED for NCSE
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reduction in electrographic seizure frequency on continuous EEG monitoring

optimal_actions.action: Obtain urgent MRI brain with gadolinium including perfusion imaging to assess for GBM recurrence
optimal_actions.expected_finding: New enhancing lesion with high rCBV at surgical cavity margin — GBM recurrence; cortical DWI ictal pseudostroke (NOT ischemic)

optimal_actions.action: Initiate continuous cEEG monitoring for 24-48 hours to track seizure burden and guide AED titration
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Progressive reduction in NCSE activity with treatment

optimal_actions.action: Escalate dexamethasone dose from 4 mg BID to 8-10 mg BID to treat increased peritumoral edema from GBM recurrence
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Reduction in peritumoral edema may reduce epileptogenicity over 24-48 hours

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Oncologic management plan for recurrent GBM

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Correct identification of ictal DWI as seizure-related, not ischemic

critical_actions: Emergent EEG to diagnose NCSE — clinical exam alone insufficient
IV lorazepam immediately followed by IV lacosamide loading for NCSE treatment
MRI brain with perfusion to diagnose GBM recurrence — CT alone insufficient
Escalate dexamethasone to treat increased peritumoral edema driving NCSE
Continuous cEEG monitoring to guide treatment and confirm seizure cessation
Do NOT administer tPA — cortical DWI changes are ictal pseudostroke, not ischemic
contraindicated_actions: Administering tPA for cortical ribbon DWI restriction — this is ictal pseudostroke from NCSE, not acute ischemic stroke
Tapering dexamethasone further — should instead be escalated given tumor recurrence with increased edema
Stopping levetiracetam — therapeutic level confirms adherence; should be maintained/escalated
Diagnosing post-ictal confusion without EEG — prolonged confusion >25 minutes requires EEG to exclude NCSE
key_reasoning_points: NCSE presenting as persistent confusion after brief convulsion requires urgent EEG — clinical distinction from post-ictal state impossible without EEG
GBM recurrence confirmed by high rCBV on perfusion MRI (not radiation necrosis) — recurrence drives seizure breakthrough
Steroid taper from 6 mg to 4 mg BID was precipitating factor — reduced edema control unmasked epileptogenic recurrent tumor
Cortical ribbon DWI restriction in active NCSE = ictal pseudostroke; does NOT represent acute ischemic stroke; tPA absolutely contraindicated
Levetiracetam therapeutic — NCSE not due to non-compliance but structural/oncologic cause requiring treatment escalation beyond AED optimization
Lacosamide is preferred second-line AED in tumor-related NCSE with right temporal origin and no cardiac contraindications
Bevacizumab for recurrent GBM may reduce seizure burden via anti-permeability (VEGF blockade reduces peritumoral edema)

metadata.teaching_points: GBM recurrence precipitating NCSE; steroid taper as precipitant; ictal pseudostroke vs ischemic stroke on DWI; high rCBV distinguishes recurrence from radiation necrosis
metadata.pitfalls: Diagnosing tPA-eligible stroke when DWI shows cortical ribbon restriction in active NCSE; failure to escalate steroids; missing GBM recurrence on non-contrast CT
metadata.clinical_pearl: In any post-craniotomy GBM patient with new confusion after seizure, EEG is mandatory. Cortical ribbon DWI = ictal, not ischemic. High rCBV on perfusion = recurrence, not radiation necrosis.
